AJ'S PERSONAL BIT: KIDS ON THE STATION ROOF
• What happened: a couple of teens, about 16, got onto the Z93 roof. No ladder. They'd gotten into parkour and climbed the pipes up the side, then stood up there looking down at you.
• You went inside: "Hey, we got kids on the roof." The answer: "Well, call the cops." Your thought: there go these kids' lives.
• You to the kids: "Dudes, what are you doing? You guys want to go to jail?"
➜ THE TAKE: Calm down a little. Yes, the internet gave you superpowers and taught you urban climbing. Be free. Go climb a hill. Go climb a tree. Plenty to climb up here. Just don't get arrested.
📞 PHONE TOPIC: What did you climb as a kid that you definitely shouldn't have? Parkour parents, how do you handle it? Text 231-929-4487.

vibe.title: Vibe Check
vibe.content:
SLOW JAM: DIDO, "THANK YOU" (2000)
• Released as a single Sept. 18, 2000, it first showed up in 1998 on the Sliding Doors soundtrack before landing on Dido's debut album No Angel.
• Chart stat: No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in April 2001, her first and only U.S. top 10, and No. 3 in the UK. Eminem's sample on "Stan" helped push it.
• Why today: Thanksgiving week, gray skies, first flakes. It's a gentle wake-up that literally says thank you.
➜ TAKE: Rain on the window, cold tea... she basically wrote the forecast for Northern Michigan this morning.
😂 JOKES: She sang "my tea's gone cold." Up here in November, so did the car. / The ultimate Thanksgiving-week song. It's called Thank You, and nobody had to sit through a speech.

🚗 DRIVE TEASE: Rain and snow showers around for the drive in, about 35 at 6 AM and 33 by 8 AM, northwest wind around 10. Wet roads, so leave a little extra room. High near 39 midday, then snow showers this afternoon with under an inch.

📅 THIS DAY: THE FIRST JUKEBOX (NOV. 23, 1889)
• On Nov. 23, 1889, the first coin-operated phonograph was installed at the Palais Royale Saloon in San Francisco.
• It was an Edison Class M electric phonograph in an oak cabinet with four stethoscope-like listening tubes, each one started by a coin. Four people could listen to the same song at once.
• Louis Glass called it the "nickel-in-the-slot player," and the saloon handed out towels so people could wipe off the tube after listening. The word "jukebox" didn't come along until much later.
➜ TAKE: 137 years later, we're still putting money into machines to hear songs. Now it's called a streaming subscription.
➜ BAIT: What song did you always play on the jukebox? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: Four people sharing one ear tube with a towel. That's the original group chat. / A nickel a song. I'd have spent my whole allowance on the same Hootie song.

💡 FUN FACT: GTA 6 VS. HUNGER GAMES
• GTA 6 made $3.79 billion in retail sales on day one, according to Take-Two.
• The new Hunger Games movie made about $120 million in its whole opening weekend, according to Boxoffice Pro.
• Do the math: GTA 6's first day was more than 31 times the biggest movie opening of the weekend.
➜ TAKE: The Hunger Games had a great weekend. GTA 6 had a great Thursday.
😂 JOKES: Thirty-one Hunger Games movies. That's a lot of volunteering as tribute. / GTA 6 made more in a day than my family will spend on Thanksgiving in the next 60 million years.

🎉 NATIONAL DAYS: National Espresso Day · National Eat a Cranberry Day · National Cashew Day

GOOD MORNING UP NORTH: First flakes of the season. Rain and snow showers this morning, about 35 at 6 AM, high near 39 midday, then snow showers this afternoon with under an inch. Tonight 28. Thanksgiving week is officially here.

SCHOOLS: No closings or delays listed this morning.

ROADS: Wet with rain and snow showers; no verified closures. South Airport westbound lane closed between Racquet Club and Park Dr for a sewer repair.

🌊 WIND & WAVES: Small Craft Advisory on Grand Traverse Bay and Lake Michigan until 4 AM Tuesday, northwest gusts to 30 knots and waves as high as about 9 feet.

ENERGY: Short week, big week. Snowbirds are state champs, Stags get their props, Lions on Thanksgiving, and everybody is one trip to the store from done.

MOOD BOOST: SIXPENCE NONE THE RICHER, "KISS ME" (1999)
• Released as a single in 1998, it took off in 1999 after the movie She's All That and the first Dawson's Creek soundtrack.

😂 JOKES: Kiss me beneath the milky twilight. Today it's beneath the milky slush. / This song made every 1999 teenager think they'd fall in love at a prom in a high school gym.

buzz.title: Daily Buzz
buzz.content:
━━ LOCAL ━━

⭐ THANK YOU, STAGS: KINGSLEY'S RUN ENDS IN THE SEMIS
• SUMMARY: Kingsley's dream season ended Saturday in Clare. Almont beat the Stags 30-6 in the Division 6 state semifinal, Kingsley's first loss of the year after a 12-0 start. The Stags scored on their very first drive, then Almont answered with 30 straight points.
• THE CATCH: It was revenge. Kingsley beat Almont for the 2023 state title at Ford Field, and Almont flipped the script three years later.
• WHO: Kingsley Stags football. WHAT: 30-6 loss in the D6 semifinal. WHERE: Clare. WHEN: Saturday. WHY IT MATTERS: 12-0, a regional title, and a whole town that drove down US-127 for them.
• WHAT'S NEXT: Almont plays Jackson Lumen Christi for the D6 title Friday at Ford Field.
➜ TAKE: Nobody in Kingsley should hang their head. Twelve straight wins, a regional title, and another semifinal. That's a program, not a fluke. Give those seniors a standing ovation.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487 with your shout-out to a Kingsley senior. We'll read 'em.
😂 JOKES: Twelve and one. Most of us can't go twelve and one with a New Year's resolution. / Almont waited three years for that rematch. That's not a grudge, that's a long-term savings plan.

SNOWBIRDS ARE STATE CHAMPS: GAYLORD ST. MARY'S FIRST TITLE
• SUMMARY: Gaylord St. Mary won the 8-player Division 2 state championship Saturday, beating Mendon 49-34 at the Superior Dome in Marquette. It's the first football state title in program history.
• THE TWIST: Their starting quarterback got hurt in the playoffs, so Cal Royce, who had played pretty much every other skill position, stepped in. Saturday he threw for 252 yards and four touchdowns, ran for 199 and three more, led the team with 13 tackles and kicked a field goal.
• QUOTE: Coach Kevin O'Connell: "Little Catholic school in northern Michigan, nobody thought we could do this, so it's pretty special."
• WHO: Gaylord St. Mary. WHAT: first state title, 49-34. WHERE: Superior Dome. WHY: a tiny Up North school just won it all.
➜ TAKE: Cal Royce had seven touchdowns, 13 tackles and a field goal. That's not a football player, that's an entire roster in one jersey.
➜ BAIT: Who's the most do-everything athlete you ever played with? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: Royce played quarterback, running back, linebacker and kicker. Somebody check if he drove the bus too. / Gaylord sent the Snowbirds north to the U.P. and they came home champions. That's the only time a snowbird flies north in November.

231 THANKSGIVING BOXES GO OUT TODAY AT NMC
• SUMMARY: NMC Professional Communications students hand out 231 Thanksgiving meal boxes today from 3:30 to 6:30 PM at the roundabout across from the Maple Lot on NMC's Front Street campus. Their goal was 215, so they blew past it.
• WHAT'S INSIDE: a turkey and traditional sides to feed a family of six, extra food for the holidays, a roasting pan, and a family activity. Gluten-free, vegetarian and vegan options too.
• WHO GETS THEM: 181 boxes go to NMC students and their families, 50 to families picked by Big Brothers Big Sisters.
• WHY: it's the 13th year of the class project called Thanks-for-Giving, which fights food insecurity and gives students real-world fundraising experience.
➜ TAKE: College students who beat their goal by 16 turkeys. These kids are going to run this town someday, and honestly, good.
➜ BAIT: Who taught you how to cook your first turkey? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: They included a roasting pan. That's thoughtful. Every family has one person who'd try to cook a turkey in a frying pan. / 231 boxes. Somebody at NMC knew exactly what area code they live in.

NMC CHOIR LANDS A NATIONAL STAGE
• SUMMARY: NMC's all-female choir Aurora was picked to perform at the American Choral Directors Association National Conference next March in Minneapolis. It's the first NMC group ever invited and the first from any Michigan community college.
• THE CATCH: only 25 groups were selected from hundreds of submissions, from children's choirs to pros.
• QUOTE: Director Jeffrey Cobb called the conference "nirvana for choir nerds" and said "there is no higher honor for a choir."
• BACKSTORY: Aurora used to be the mixed Chamber Singers. Cobb rebuilt it as an all-treble choir four years ago because he couldn't recruit enough men.
➜ TAKE: Our community college just got picked over hundreds of choirs across the country. Traverse City, keep sending us your talent.
➜ BAIT: Were you a choir kid? What song do you still know every harmony to? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: Couldn't find enough guys for the choir, so he built an all-women group and it went national. Fellas, that's on you. / Nirvana for choir nerds. Not the band. Please don't show up in flannel.

ROTARY SQUARE GETS ITS BUILDER (YES, IT'S AJ'S)
• SUMMARY: The Traverse City DDA approved more than $3.4 million in contracts Friday to build Rotary Square downtown. Groundbreaking is planned for April, with completion by November next year.
• THE TWIST: the low bid came from AJ's Excavating at about $2.85 million. The other bid was about $6.2 million.
• WHAT IT'LL HAVE: a big central lawn, swing benches, a raised walkway with a slide, a shaded stage area, native plantings, and a riverwalk path connecting to FishPass.
• WHY IT MATTERS: the civic square has been in the works for over 30 years. The design is called Petoskey Stone.
➜ TAKE: For the record, I am not getting a cut. But if there's a slide, I'm going down it on opening day.
➜ BAIT: What should be the first event in Rotary Square? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: AJ's Excavating got the job. I want it on record I can't even dig out my driveway. / Thirty years in the making. That's longer than it takes to find parking downtown, but only barely.

━━ NATIONAL ━━

HUNGER GAMES OPENS TO $120 MILLION
• SUMMARY: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened at No. 1 with about $120 million this weekend, the franchise's fourth-best start, roughly tied with Mockingjay Part 1. It's about $225 million worldwide.
• THE CATCH: it's an estimate, and Monday's actual numbers could move it up a spot in the franchise rankings.
• WHY YOU CARE: it's the movie everybody's crew went to this weekend, and it's still going strong into the Thanksgiving holiday.
➜ TAKE: Thanksgiving week plan: watch kids fight to the death on screen, then go home and watch your family fight over the last roll.
➜ BAIT: Did you see it this weekend? Book people, was it as good as the book? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: $120 million. May the odds be ever in your favor at the concession stand. / It's called Sunrise on the Reaping. At 6 AM in November, I'm still waiting for my sunrise.

MILEY CYRUS GOT MARRIED
• SUMMARY: Miley Cyrus married drummer Maxx Morando Saturday in a poolside ceremony in Palm Springs. Wayne Coyne from the Flaming Lips officiated.
• THE DETAILS: she wore a long-sleeved white satin gown and was photographed wiping away tears during the vows. Guests included Tish Cyrus, Noah Cyrus and Billy Ray Cyrus.
• THE CATCH: it came one month after the two sang "Let's Get Married" together on stage at the Hollywood Bowl.
➜ TAKE: She told us a month ago. She literally sang "Let's Get Married" at the Hollywood Bowl. Nobody can say they didn't see this coming.
➜ BAIT: Would you do a poolside wedding in November? What's the best wedding you've ever been to? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: A wedding officiated by the guy from the Flaming Lips. I hope the vows came with confetti cannons. / Billy Ray was there. Somewhere, an achy breaky heart got a little less achy.

━━ BITS ━━

FIRST SNOW SHOWERS: WHAT'S YOUR FIRST-SNOW RULE?
• NWS says rain and snow showers this morning, then snow showers this afternoon. Less than an inch for Traverse City, temps sliding from the upper 30s.
• MLive says the cold front drops temps statewide and brings the first real snow to parts of Michigan.
• The bit: everyone has a first-snow rule. Snow tires on? Scraper back in the car? Is the first snow a hot-chocolate day by law?
➜ TAKE: My first-snow rule: the ice scraper is in the trunk, buried under summer stuff. Every year.
➜ BAIT: What's your first-snow rule? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: First snow means one thing up here: everybody forgets how to drive for exactly one day. / Somebody in Traverse City is still in shorts today, and we respect it.

NATIONAL ESPRESSO DAY: HOW DO YOU TAKE IT?
• Today is National Espresso Day, plus National Cashew Day and National Eat a Cranberry Day, per National Day Calendar.
• The bit: what's your coffee order, and what does it say about you? Black coffee people, latte people, and people whose order takes 30 seconds to say.
➜ TAKE: If your order has more than four words, you're not ordering coffee, you're reading a novel.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487 your full coffee order, exactly how you say it at the window.
😂 JOKES: A shot of espresso on a snowy Monday isn't a drink. It's a life jacket. / Espresso, cashews and cranberries. That's not three national days, that's a trail mix.

• Aydrian Day, a 16-year-old from the Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians who goes to school in Leelanau County, beaded his first barrette for his mom at age three.
• Two of his pieces are now on exhibit in Best of Show: Making History at Santa Fe Indian Market at the Museum of Indian Arts and Culture, on display through March 2027.
• He's made moccasins, earrings, cradleboards and full regalia, and credits everything to his mom, who let him watch and try his own styles.
• His message: "From old to young, it's never too late to learn."

gta6.content:

• CONFIRMED (Take-Two, Nov 20): GTA 6 did $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales, which Take-Two calls a record for entertainment in any medium.

lifestyle.title: Lifestyle & Trends
lifestyle.content:
THANKSGIVING DINNER FOR 10: $58.63
• The American Farm Bureau's annual survey puts a classic Thanksgiving dinner for 10 at $58.63 this year, about $5.86 per person, up about 6 percent from last year.
• Turkey is the big driver, up about 10 percent, because flocks are still recovering from disease.
• Good news for pie people: pie crust and whipped cream are cheaper, and celery and carrots are down too. The Farm Bureau's tip: watch the store ads, because grocers want your Thanksgiving business.
➜ LOCAL ANGLE: Up North, a lot of us are hosting this week, and with turkey up 10 percent, the store flyers in your mailbox are worth a look before you shop.
➜ TAKE: Six bucks a person. Cheaper than a fancy coffee, and that coffee doesn't come with leftovers.
➜ BAIT: What's the one Thanksgiving dish you'd pay double for? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: Turkey went up 10 percent. The turkey would like you to know it's not thrilled about the price either. / Pie crust and whipped cream got cheaper. Finally, the economy is listening to me.

81.5 MILLION HIT THE ROAD FOR THANKSGIVING
• AAA projects 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles for Thanksgiving, Tuesday through next Monday, just under last year's record.
• That ends a three-year streak of record Thanksgiving travel. AAA says higher travel costs are part of it, including record gas prices in August, September and October.
• Almost 90 percent of travelers will drive, and AAA says check tires, batteries and fluids before you go.
➜ LOCAL ANGLE: Up North, with snow showers in the mix this week, checking tires and wipers before Grandma's house isn't optional.
➜ TAKE: 81.5 million people traveling and every single one of them will be in front of you at the gas station on Wednesday.
➜ BAIT: Are you hosting or traveling this year? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: Ending a three-year record streak. Thanksgiving travel finally took a year off. Lucky. / Ninety percent driving. That's a lot of 'are we there yet' per mile.

officeschool.title: Office & School Bits
officeschool.content:
OFFICE: FEWER OF US GET THANKSGIVING OFF
• A new YouGov poll says 58 percent of working Americans get Thanksgiving Day off, down from 68 percent last year.
• And 19 percent say they'll work a full day or limited hours on Thanksgiving, up from 14 percent.
➜ TAKE: If you're working Thursday, you're the real hero. And you get first pick of the leftovers. That's the law.
➜ BAIT: Who's working Thanksgiving? Text 231-929-4487 and tell us where.
😂 JOKES: Working Thanksgiving means you skip the political debate at the table. Some people call that a perk. / Your boss scheduled you Thursday? Bring him a plate. A small one.

OFFICE: THE GTA 6 SICK DAY WAS REAL
• HR platform BambooHR looked at time-off data for more than 3.4 million U.S. workers: requests for GTA 6 launch day, Nov. 19, ran about 13 percent higher than a normal year, and the bump carried into Friday.
• In the same research, 18 percent of salaried workers said they planned to take launch day off, including 32 percent of Gen Z.
➜ TAKE: If your coworker 'had a cold' last Thursday and showed up Monday with no sleep and a big smile, you know.
➜ BAIT: Did anybody at your work mysteriously take Thursday off? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: One in three Gen Z workers planned to take the day off. The other two just played it at their desks. / Calling in sick for a video game. In my day we called in sick for Opening Day like normal people.

SCHOOL: PARENTS WANT AI TAUGHT, WITH GUARDRAILS
• A National Parents Union survey found 77 percent of parents want K-12 schools to teach kids how to use AI tools well, and 85 percent want AI safety taught.
• Only 46 percent think their state is handling technology in schools well enough. Parents say they want measured rules, not total bans, plus more teacher training.
➜ TAKE: We used to get in trouble for using a calculator. Now kids are getting graded on how they use a robot.
➜ BAIT: Parents, is your kid using AI for homework, and do you check? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: My kid asked AI to do his homework. AI asked for an extension. / Teaching AI safety in school. Step one: do not let it write your excuse note.

SCHOOL: CENTRAL GRADE'S BLACK FRIDAY AUCTION
• Central Grade School's PTO online auction opens at 8 AM on Black Friday, Nov. 27, and runs until 8:30 PM Dec. 5.
• An adults-only party follows from 7 to 9:30 PM Dec. 5 at Right Brain Brewery.
➜ TAKE: Black Friday shopping that actually helps your kid's school? Finally, a doorbuster I can feel good about.
➜ BAIT: What's the best thing you ever won at a school auction? Text 231-929-4487.
😂 JOKES: A bidding war for a good cause. Just don't get outbid by the gym teacher. They're competitive. / Adults-only party at a brewery for the PTO. That's the most honest name for a parent meeting I've ever heard.

mental.title: Mental Health Minute
mental.content:
MAKE ONE IF-THEN PLAN FOR THE SNOW

First real flakes are coming down today, and it's Thanksgiving week, so there's a lot riding on your brain right now: the roads, the groceries, who's bringing what, and whether the scraper is even in the car. When everything piles up like that, our heads try to hold it all at once, and that's exactly what makes us feel frazzled. So here's one small move that researchers have tested in a lot of studies. Pick one thing that's stressing you, and make an if-then plan for it. If it's snowing when I walk out tomorrow, then I leave ten minutes early. If the store's out of my brand of stuffing, then I grab the store brand and move on. Say it out loud once, right now, while you're sitting at this light. A big review of 94 studies found that people who set plans like that, a when and a then, actually followed through on their goals a lot more often than people who just meant to. You decide once, and then you don't have to decide again when you're cold and in a hurry. That's one less thing to carry this week. Text me your if-then at 231-929-4487, and I'll read a few. You've got this.

flash.content:
LINGER — THE CRANBERRIES
• Released as a single: Feb. 15, 1993 (second single from Everybody Else Is Doing It, So Why Can't We?; re-released Jan. 31, 1994; first heard on a 1990 Ireland-only demo)

An early version came out in 1990 on a demo tape when the band was still called The Cranberry Saw Us.

lifestyle.title: THANKSGIVING DINNER FOR 10: $58.63
lifestyle.summary: The American Farm Bureau's annual survey puts a classic Thanksgiving dinner for 10 at $58.63 this year, about $5.86 per person, up about 6 percent from last year. Turkey is the big driver, up about 10 percent, because flocks are still recovering from disease. Good news for pie people: pie crust and whipped cream are cheaper, and celery and carrots are down too. The Farm Bureau's tip: watch the store ads, because grocers want your Thanksgiving business.
lifestyle.article_title: Farm Bureau Survey Shows Thanksgiving Cost Higher in 2026 (American Farm Bureau Federation)

lifestyle.title: 81.5 MILLION HIT THE ROAD FOR THANKSGIVING
lifestyle.summary: AAA projects 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles for Thanksgiving, Tuesday through next Monday, just under last year's record. That ends a three-year streak of record Thanksgiving travel. AAA says higher travel costs are part of it, including record gas prices in August, September and October. Almost 90 percent of travelers will drive, and AAA says check tires, batteries and fluids before you go.
lifestyle.article_title: Thanksgiving Travel Expected to Dip Slightly Compared to Last Year (AAA Newsroom, Nov 16)

officeSchool.summary: HR platform BambooHR looked at time-off data for more than 3.4 million U.S. workers: requests for GTA 6 launch day, Nov. 19, ran about 13 percent higher than a normal year, and the bump carried into Friday. In the same research, 18 percent of salaried workers said they planned to take launch day off, including 32 percent of Gen Z.
officeSchool.article_title: GTA 6 Day: Lessons in Planning Office Attendance Around Predictable Dips (Hubstar)

officeSchool.title: SCHOOL: PARENTS WANT AI TAUGHT, WITH GUARDRAILS
officeSchool.summary: A National Parents Union survey found 77 percent of parents want K-12 schools to teach kids how to use AI tools well, and 85 percent want AI safety taught. Only 46 percent think their state is handling technology in schools well enough. Parents say they want measured rules, not total bans, plus more teacher training.
officeSchool.article_title: Survey: Most Parents Want Students to Use AI in School, With Strong Safeguards (EdSurge, Nov 3)
